page0.text:
I turn off the lights in the house.
It's four in the morning.
We leave the Emiya residence with a few hours left until dawn.

page1.text:
We have our plan.
There's nothing else to discuss. Now we just need to go to the battlefield and carry out each of our responsibilities.

page2.text:
...There's no guarantee we'll come back safely.
Well, until now it's been a recurring event, but this time there is no guarantee we'll return.
So I need to make sure to turn off all of the lights in my house.

page3.text:
"...Huh?"
Someone's standing in the garden.
A blonde girl gazes up at the night sky, doing nothing in particular.

page4.text:
"Hey! What are you up to, Saber?"
"I was looking at the sky, and this house."
She answers me in a very gentle voice.
When we first met, she looked at this house with a different expression.

page5.text:
"So much has happened. I want to burn it into my memory, so that I always remember."
...
Her voice...
It reflects a determination that she might never come back, even greater than mine.

page6.text:
"Yeah? ...Well, remember it as long as you can."
I make a humble request of her from the windowed hallway.

page7.text:
"Yes. I have a favor to ask of you as well.
I will protect you. So please, make sure you both return to this house."
"Yeah. We will."

page8.text:
That's the only answer I can give now.
We're going to destroy the Holy Grail. When that happens, Saber will leave too because she's a Servant.

page9.text:
I'd like her to stay here,
and she's even developed an attachment to our home.
But that's a rule she can't break as long as she's a Servant.

page10.text:
"Hey, what are you two doing!? We need to hurry, there isn't much time!"
A voice beckons us from the front door.
Tohsaka seems to have finished preparations and is already at the gate.

page11.text:
"Let us be off, Shirou."
"Yeah. Time to finish this, Saber."
I turn off the last light, and leave the house with Saber.

page12.text:
The night is quiet.
In the garden, under the starry sky, the illusion of a girl gazing up at the stars still remains.

page13.text:
Our direction is set.
Saber's going to breach Ryudou Temple from the front gate, while Tohsaka and I will infiltrate from the back of the mountain.

page14.text:
We plan to have Saber enter the temple slightly sooner than us to draw Gilgamesh's attention.
We'll use the opening to sneak into Ryudou Temple from the back, stop the Holy Grail as soon as possible, and then back Saber up.

page15.text:
...Then, I'll counter Gilgamesh's Noble Phantasm with my Projection, so Saber can close in and finish him off.
That's our only strategy right now.

page16.text:
...
There's a barely intact path in the hills behind the temple.
Tohsaka scales the slope as surely as if she'd scoped out the area beforehand.

page17.text:
At night, the mountains are dark and sinister.
The mountain is an inviolable and spiritual ground, so it naturally repels us.
While the dark mountain itself is dangerous to human hikers, it also embodies a sacred realm with high spiritual purity.
However...

page18.text:
"...This isn't normal. The air's so fishy it's making me nauseous."
Tohsaka gags, squinting at Ryudou Temple at the summit.
"Fishy" is just her figure of speech.
There isn't actually a fishy smell coming from the mountain.
It just feels bizarre.
The air feels uncomfortably lukewarm, and it sticks to my skin.

page19.text:
The life energy in the air feels so raw, I can't tell if I'm breathing or the mountain's breathing.
I even hallucinate that we're hiking up a giant intestine, not a mountain.

page20.text:
"...I should have asked sooner, but how do you feel, Shirou?"
Suddenly,
Tohsaka asked me how I was.

page21.text:
"Huh? Well, not 'good' or 'bad,'
honestly, I have so much that I don't know what to do with all this."

page22.text:
I tell her my honest feelings.
With this much magical energy, ten or twenty Projections would be a piece of cake.
But you could compare it to putting a jet engine on a worn-out plane. I feel like I can't relax, as if I'll spring a fuel leak and explode if I lose focus.

page23.text:
"Wow, that's a nice problem to have. I'm glad it worked out, though. I was worried because it was my first time."
"Worried? Don't tell me that was actually a really risky ritual?"
"Not the process, but the aftermath.
I have to balance the energy I share with you with the energy Saber takes. You know Saber's output is lower because I have to juggle you both, right?"

page24.text: "Ah... Right, that's true. Then Saber can't fight the way she wants?"

page25.text:
"Hey, don't underestimate me.
I'm not that sloppy, and I'm not giving you much power compared to Saber, so it'll work itself out.
Still, we can't be reckless. Saber can only use her sacred sword once right now."

page26.text:
"She can only use it once?"
...Then she can't use it on Gilgamesh.
We need Saber's Noble Phantasm to destroy the Holy Grail.

page27.text: "Then, Saber's going to stop Gilgamesh without her trump card!?"

page28.text:
"Yeah. That's why we need to regroup with her as soon as possible.
Saber said that she'll use her sacred sword once she determines that she can't stop Gilgamesh.
...But if she does that, she's finished. She can't destroy the Holy Grail without it.
So when that happens..."

page29.text:
...
He holds his breath.
When that happens...
She's prepared to use the sacred sword knowing that she'll disappear afterward.

page30.text:
"Tohsaka, you mean..."
"...We don't really have a choice. It was Saber's idea. She'll destroy the Holy Grail even if I try to stop her."
Tohsaka doesn't look at me as she murmurs.

page31.text:
...
...Damn it. What a fool she is.
This is just as hard on Tohsaka.
She doesn't want Saber to disappear, either.
Then...

page32.text:
"Let's hurry. I won't let Gilgamesh have Saber."
"Of course not. Saber belongs to me. I won't let a guy like that kill her."
